text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.66% today as crude oil prices dropped sharply on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. Crude fell to $103.37 per barrel in the US market—a meaningful pullback after climbing above $154 just four trading days ago—on signals that both the US and Iranian presidents are open to negotiation rather than escalation. Lower oil prices directly hit the earnings outlook for oil producers like this company.

The decline also reflects broader political uncertainty following the midterm elections, where Democrats look poised to take control of Congress. A Democratic-led government is generally seen as more supportive of renewable energy like offshore wind and solar, which could reduce long-term demand for fossil fuels and pressure oil prices further over time.
